References / Poster / 396

Worker Men and Women:
Everyone Vote in the Soviet Elections

Gustav Klutsis multiplies one photographed raised hand into a crowd of hands and sets the slogan in white capitals on the diagonal across a solid red field.

Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Art Institute of Chicago records the poster as color offset lithograph on cream wove paper, 119.7 × 84.7 cm, 1930, and marks it as not in the public domain. Art Institute of Chicago.

The same museum holds a 1930 gelatin silver print with red gouache by Klutsis, We Shall Fulfill the Country’s Coal Debt (2011.872), which shares its title with his 1930 poster (2011.865) and shows the photographic stage of his method.

Observed

  • The ground is a solid red from edge to edge.
  • A giant photographed hand, cut out along its outline, rises diagonally from the lower right to the upper left and fills most of the sheet.
  • At its wrist, the hand dissolves into a photomontage of many smaller raised hands and faces of workers.
  • “РАБОЧИЕ и РАБОТНИЦЫ” runs down to the right in white condensed capitals, with oversized initial letters.
  • “ВСЕ НА ПЕРЕВЫБОРЫ СОВЕТОВ” runs up to the right at the lower left on the same diagonal, ending in a large “СОВЕТОВ”.
  • The signature “КЛУЦИС” runs vertically in small capitals at the right edge.
  • The only hue is the red; the photographs are black and white, and the type is the cream of the paper.

Why it belongs

Here red is the whole ground, not an accent, which is the upper end of the style’s range for chromatic area. The poster shows the style at its most photographic, about 1930.

The single hand that becomes many hands is the core device of Klutsis’s photomontage: repetition and scale turn a document into a slogan.

Borrow

Use one full-bleed red field with a single large cut-out photograph and white type.

Set a two-part slogan on one diagonal axis, one part above and one below the image, with oversized initials.
